{{Lowercase title}}
In [[probability theory]], the '''g-expectation''' is a [[nonlinear expectation]] based on a backwards [[stochastic differential equation]] (BSDE) originally developed by [[Shige Peng]].<ref name=BCHMP>{{cite journal |title=A Converse Comparison Theorem for BSDEs and Related Properties of g-Expectation |author1=Philippe Briand |author2=François Coquet |author3=Ying Hu |author4=Jean Mémin |author5=Shige Peng |journal=Electronic Communications in Probability |year=2000 |volume=5 |issue=13 |pages=101–117 |url=http://www.emis.de/journals/EJP-ECP/_ejpecp/ECP/include/getdoc721b.pdf }}</ref>

== Definition ==
Given a probability space <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})</math> with <math>(W_t)_{t \geq 0}</math> is a (''d''-dimensional) [[Wiener process]] (on that space).  Given the [[filtration (probability theory)|filtration]] generated by <math>(W_t)</math>, i.e. <math>\mathcal{F}_t = \sigma(W_s: s \in [0,t])</math>, let <math>X</math> be <math>\mathcal{F}_T</math> [[measurable]].  Consider the BSDE given by:
:<math> \begin{align}dY_t &= g(t,Y_t,Z_t) \, dt - Z_t \, dW_t\\ Y_T &= X\end{align}</math>
Then the g-expectation for <math>X</math> is given by <math>\mathbb{E}^g[X] := Y_0</math>.  Note that if <math>X</math> is an ''m''-dimensional vector, then <math>Y_t</math> (for each time <math>t</math>) is an ''m''-dimensional vector and <math>Z_t</math> is an <math>m \times d</math> matrix.

In fact the [[conditional expectation]] is given by <math>\mathbb{E}^g[X \mid \mathcal{F}_t] := Y_t</math> and much like the formal definition for conditional expectation it follows that <math>\mathbb{E}^g[1_A \mathbb{E}^g[X \mid \mathcal{F}_t]] = \mathbb{E}^g[1_A X]</math> for any <math>A \in \mathcal{F}_t</math> (and the <math>1</math> function is the [[indicator function]]).<ref name=BCHMP />

== Existence and uniqueness ==
Let <math>g: [0,T] \times \mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^{m \times d} \to \mathbb{R}^m</math>  satisfy:
# <math>g(\cdot,y,z)</math> is an <math>\mathcal{F}_t</math>-[[adapted process]] for every <math>(y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}</math>
# <math>\int_0^T |g(t,0,0)| \, dt \in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal{F}_T,\mathbb{P})</math> the [[Lp space|L2 space]] (where <math>| \cdot |</math> is a norm in <math>\mathbb{R}^m</math>)
# <math>g</math> is [[Lipschitz continuous]] in <math>(y,z)</math>, i.e. for every <math>y_1,y_2 \in \mathbb{R}^m</math> and <math>z_1,z_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}</math> it follows that <math>|g(t,y_1,z_1) - g(t,y_2,z_2)| \leq C (|y_1 - y_2| + |z_1 - z_2|)</math> for some constant <math>C</math>
Then for any random variable <math>X \in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal{F}_t,\mathbb{P};\mathbb{R}^m)</math> there exists a unique pair of <math>\mathcal{F}_t</math>-adapted processes <math>(Y,Z)</math> which satisfy the stochastic differential equation.<ref name=Peng04>{{Cite book | last1 = Peng | first1 = S. | chapter = Nonlinear Expectations, Nonlinear Evaluations and Risk Measures | doi = 10.1007/978-3-540-44644-6_4 | title = Stochastic Methods in Finance | series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics | volume = 1856 | pages = 165–138 | year = 2004 | isbn = 978-3-540-22953-7 | url = http://sisla06.samsi.info/fmse/pm/ShigePeng.pdf | format = pdf | access-date = August 9, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160303223024/http://sisla06.samsi.info/fmse/pm/ShigePeng.pdf | archive-date = March 3, 2016 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

In particular, if <math>g</math> additionally satisfies:
# <math>g</math> is continuous in time (<math>t</math>)
# <math>g(t,y,0) \equiv 0</math> for all <math>(t,y) \in [0,T] \times \mathbb{R}^m</math>
then for the terminal random variable <math>X \in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal{F}_t,\mathbb{P};\mathbb{R}^m)</math> it follows that the solution processes <math>(Y,Z)</math> are square integrable.  Therefore <math>\mathbb{E}^g[X | \mathcal{F}_t]</math> is square integrable for all times <math>t</math>.<ref name="Choquet+g-expectation">{{Cite journal | last1 = Chen | first1 = Z. | last2 = Chen | first2 = T. | last3 = Davison | first3 = M. | doi = 10.1214/009117904000001053 | title = Choquet expectation and Peng's g -expectation | journal = The Annals of Probability | volume = 33 | issue = 3 | pages = 1179 | year = 2005 | arxiv = math/0506598 }}</ref>
